problem:
Calculate the volume of the $4$-dimensional parallelepiped spanned by the vectors

$$
a=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ -2 \\ 4\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,c=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,d=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ 4 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

examples.knowledge_point: Computing the Volume of an N-Dimensional Parallelepiped
examples.problem:
Calculate the volume of the $4$-dimensional parallelepiped spanned by the vectors

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14081590/assets/c185678d20cabf2a302c0101876f9fb67fd35cf682f547f62a9eeb99fd97946f.png)
examples.worked_solution:
First, let's construct the matrix $M,$ whose columns are the coordinates of our vectors $\mathbf{a},$ $\mathbf{b},$ $\mathbf{c},$ and  $\mathbf{d}{:}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14081590/assets/923b0fb4f65d4de6538658d49e32fb3256fd374b1cc94dd62256f9e966c72d24.png)

The volume of the parallelepiped spanned by these vectors equals the absolute value of the determinant of $M{:}$

$$
V = | \det(M) |
$$

Notice that the $2$nd row of the determinant contains three zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $2$nd row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M) & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & -2 & 1 \\ 3 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 5 & -4 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot (-1)^{2+1}|\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3|\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the $2$nd row of the $3 \times 3$ determinant contains two zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $2$nd row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M) & =-3|\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3\cdot 1\cdot (-1)^{2+2}|\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ -4 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3|\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ -4 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3(15+4) \\  & =-57.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume is

$$
V = | \det(M) | = |-57| = 57.
$$

feedback.problem:
Find the determinant of the matrix 
$B=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 6 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 1 & 2 & 8 \\ 9 & 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}].$
feedback.worked_solution:
Notice that the $3$rd column contains three zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $3$rd column, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B) & =|\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 6 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 1 & 2 & 8 \\ 9 & 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{3+3}|\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 6 & 0 \\ 9 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot |\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 6 & 0 \\ 9 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of a triangular matrix is equal to the product of the entries on the main diagonal. Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}2\cdot |\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 6 & 0 \\ 9 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}| & =2\cdot 5\cdot 6\cdot (-1)=-60.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
det(B)=-60.
$$
